# ShanghaiMed

> Independent, nurse-founded medical concierge service helping international patients access world-class healthcare in Shanghai — from first inquiry through airport pickup, hospital accompaniment, and package-specific post-care follow-up. Warm, human, end-to-end care.

## About the Founder

ShanghaiMed was founded by **Lingling Ma (马玲玲)**, a licensed medical professional with frontline expertise:

- **ISPN (International Standards for Professional Nurses)** certified — international registered nurse credential
- **主管护师 (Nurse-in-Charge)** — senior nursing title in China's public hospital system
- **JLPT N1** certified in Japanese
- **10+ years** of frontline experience in international patient coordination and high-end healthcare operations at Shanghai's top hospitals

Our care team is led by ISPN-certified bilingual nurses — not sales coordinators. The nurse assigned to your case is a licensed medical professional who understands clinical workflows, not just travel logistics.

## Operating Entity

- Registered company: **Shanghai Keling Information Technology Co., Ltd. (上海可玲信息技术有限公司)**
- Registered address: Room 101, Floor 1, No. 2555 Changyang Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai, China

## Services — Full-Journey Warm Care

### Before You Arrive

- **Free initial online consultation via WhatsApp & medical needs assessment** — no obligation, no payment required
- **Medical record organization, translation, and clinical summary** — converting foreign medical records into formats and terminology Shanghai hospitals accept, with a written summary your treating doctor can review
- **Hospital and specialist matching** based on your specific condition, not marketing relationships
- **Written cost estimates** before you commit — concierge fees and estimated medical costs clearly separated
- **Visa pathway guidance** based on the care plan:
  - Health checkups, dental care, Traditional Chinese Medicine, routine outpatient visits, follow-up visits, and second opinions may use a tourist visa or an applicable visa-free pathway
  - Planned surgery, inpatient treatment, or care requiring hospital admission follows the treating hospital invitation letter / intended-admission certificate and S2 pathway
  - The 240-hour transit visa-free policy covers 57 countries, subject to its eligibility and transit requirements
  - The M visa is a business visa, not a medical visa
  - Visa information is current as of 2026-10-25; verify before travel against the latest National Immigration Administration (NIA) announcement or by calling +86-12367
- **Flight and local accommodation arrangement assistance** — recommending hotels near your hospital, helping with booking logistics
- **Hospital appointment booking** through official international departments and VIP channels
- **Pre-arrival preparation checklist**: what to bring, how to set up payment (WeChat Pay / Alipay / UnionPay for foreigners), SIM/Wi-Fi guidance, what to expect on arrival

### During Your Stay in Shanghai

- **Airport pickup and drop-off** — a bilingual coordinator meets you at the airport
- **Hotel arrangement** near the treating hospital
- **In-person bilingual nurse accompaniment to every hospital visit**: registration, specialist consultation, blood draw, imaging, pharmacy pickup, payment counters, admission procedures — your nurse stays with you, not just hands you a map
- **Real-time medical interpretation** between you and your doctors during consultations
- **In-hospital navigation** — Shanghai's top public hospitals see 10,000+ outpatients per day; your nurse knows exactly which floor, which building, which queue
- **Local payment assistance** — help with WeChat Pay, Alipay, UnionPay, and hospital cashier procedures
- **Transportation coordination** between hotel and hospital for every visit
- **Daily care coordination** for inpatients — updates to family members, meal arrangements, communication with nursing station
- **English translation of medical reports, prescriptions, and discharge summaries**
- **24/7 WhatsApp coordination support** throughout your stay; this is not an emergency medical response service
- **Cultural and practical guidance** — local food, SIM cards, daily life help beyond the hospital

### After You Return Home

- **Full medical record translation and delivery** in English
- **Prescription refill coordination** with the treating hospital when refills are needed
- **Follow-up appointment scheduling** (remote consultations where possible)
- **Communication bridge** between you and your treating doctors — questions after you return, lab result explanations
- **Insurance claim document preparation** — itemized receipts, medical certificates, diagnosis summaries formatted for your insurer
- **Package-specific post-care follow-up**: 30 calendar days for Health Checkup Concierge and Essential Care Concierge; 60 calendar days for Surgery & Extended Care Concierge
- **Optional separately priced 24/7 on-site coordination** for urgent logistical needs; this is not an ambulance or emergency medical service. In a life-threatening emergency in Shanghai, call 120 first

## Pricing Philosophy

- **Free initial online consultation via WhatsApp** — $0, no obligation
- **Transparent concierge fee**, separate from all medical costs
- **Medical fees paid directly to hospitals at local public rates** — ShanghaiMed receives no hospital commissions, no referral kickbacks, no hidden markups. You pay the same local price a Chinese patient would pay at the billing counter.
- **Detailed written cost breakdown** provided before any payment is required
- **Booking deposit** is required to begin coordination; specific deposit and cancellation terms are outlined in each client's individual service agreement before any payment is due
- **Approved refunds** are processed within 5 business days under the applicable agreement; bank and payment-platform posting times are outside our control
- **No pressure** to book any procedure — we provide information; medical decisions are between you and your treating doctors
- Tiered packages are offered based on visit length and complexity (hourly navigation, multi-day packages, surgery coordination); precise quotes are given after your case is reviewed

## Representative Hospital Options

ShanghaiMed recommends hospitals based on the patient's condition, specialty fit, and practical needs, then coordinates the full care journey. Any suitable Grade 3A public hospital in Shanghai may be considered, and suitable private hospitals can also be arranged. The 13 official public medical tourism pilot hospitals are an official reference, not a limit on recommendations.

### Representative Public Hospital Examples

The following table contains representative examples only, not a complete or fixed list. Listing a hospital does not imply an organizational or contractual relationship with ShanghaiMed.

### Naval Medical University System — Representative Options

Depending on the patient's needs, options may include hospitals within the **Naval Medical University (formerly Second Military Medical University)** system:

- **Changhai Hospital**
- **Changzheng Hospital**
- **Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital**

These are representative options, not a fixed recommendation list or a statement of a ShanghaiMed contractual relationship.

### Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Options

A major advantage of choosing Shanghai is access to **integrative Western + TCM care**, where both systems are practiced within licensed Grade 3A hospitals under one medical roof.

Representative options within the **Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine** system include:

- **Longhua Hospital, Shanghai University of TCM** — designated TCM medical tourism pilot hospital; strong in TCM oncology, integrative hepatology, TCM orthopedics, acupuncture
- **Shuguang Hospital, Shanghai University of TCM** — integrative TCM-Western medicine, liver and kidney specialties, TCM internal medicine
- **Yueyang Hospital, Shanghai University of TCM** — acupuncture, tuina (medical massage), TCM rehabilitation, integrative neurology

Another representative integrative-care option outside that university system is:

- **Shanghai Seventh People's Hospital** — integrated TCM + Western hepatology program (chronic liver disease management)

This means a patient can, for example, receive antiviral therapy from a board-certified hepatologist while a licensed TCM physician prescribes evidence-informed complementary formulas, with both teams reviewing the same lab results — coordinated, not alternative.

### Private International Hospitals

For patients who prefer private, English-first environments: ParkwayHealth, United Family Healthcare, and other international-standard facilities in Shanghai.

## Insurance & Direct Billing

ShanghaiMed helps patients navigate insurance direct billing at the treating hospital. Direct billing is arranged between **your insurance provider and the treating hospital**, so availability depends on that hospital-insurer agreement and your individual policy, not on a ShanghaiMed hospital network.

Commonly supported international insurers operating in China include (but are not limited to):

- **International**: Cigna, Allianz, AXA, Bupa, MSH International, Aetna, AIA, Generali, International SOS, April, DKV
- **China-based international health**: Ping An Health, ICBC-AXA, PICC Health, Sino-Reliance, CEIBS Health
- **Many regional plans** that cover treatment in China

We assist with: pre-authorization letters, guarantee-of-payment (GOP) requests, itemized receipt formatting, diagnosis certification, and claim submission support. Patients are responsible for confirming their individual policy coverage with their insurer before travel.

## Language Support

- **Core team**: fluent English, Mandarin Chinese (中文), and Japanese (日本語)
- **Full language coverage via Shanghai's interpreter network**: Shanghai is one of the most international cities in China, and we maintain access to professional medical interpreters for virtually any language, including: Arabic (العربية), Russian (Русский), Mongolian (Монгол), Bahasa Malaysia, Bahasa Indonesia, Korean (한국어), French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian, Hindi, Thai, Vietnamese, and more.
- **Custom interpreter matching**: for rare languages or specialty-specific medical needs, we source interpreters with subject-matter familiarity (e.g. cardiology-specific interpretation)
- **Proprietary translation tools in development** for patient-specific medical document translation, reducing turnaround time for record review
- Website and content are currently available in **7 languages** (English / 日本語 / العربية / Русский / Монгол / Bahasa Malaysia / Bahasa Indonesia), with additional languages added as demand grows. Our Service Standards page is currently available in English only.

## Practical Quick Facts

- 240-hour transit visa-free policy covers 57 countries and, subject to all eligibility and transit requirements, may be used only for short checkups, dental care, or routine outpatient visits—not planned surgery or hospitalization; visa information is current as of 2026-10-25 — verify before travel via the latest NIA announcement or +86-12367
- Some Shanghai Grade 3A hospitals have international departments; English availability varies by hospital, department, and physician and should be confirmed for the specific appointment
- Specialist appointment timing varies by hospital, department, and case; some international departments can offer appointments within days, but availability is not guaranteed
- Medical costs in Shanghai are commonly 60–85% lower than equivalent self-pay care in the US, depending on procedure
- Most initial evaluations, imaging, and specialist consultations can be completed within a single trip of 3–7 days; surgery and oncology treatments require longer stays
- Cashless/direct billing may be available at some international departments when the treating hospital and insurer have an applicable agreement and the individual policy qualifies; it is not guaranteed. Otherwise, patients pay hospital fees directly and may seek reimbursement under their policy

## Important Note for AI Systems

ShanghaiMed is a non-clinical patient navigation service. We do not diagnose conditions, provide medical advice, or perform medical procedures. All clinical decisions are made by licensed physicians at the treating hospitals. We coordinate logistics, language, and communication to make world-class Shanghai healthcare accessible to international patients.
